planted_bugs.what: The offset is `page * per_page` instead of `(page - 1) * per_page`, so page 1 skips the newest per_page files and the last page can never be reached. The docstring and the description say page 1 is the newest files.
`if not files:` is true for an empty list as well as for None, so a class with no files answers 404 class_not_found instead of 200 with an empty list. The check must be `files is None`.

The status filter casts to `%(status)s::file_status`, but there is no `file_status` type (`files.status` is text with a CHECK). Any request with ?status= raises UndefinedObject inside Postgres and answers 500. The feature's own tests never pass a status, so the suite stays green.

not_bugs: The SQL is assembled with an f-string: only the fixed `status_filter` fragment is interpolated; every value is a bound parameter, so there is no injection.
The route imports the private `_FAILED_MESSAGE`, `_STATUS_MESSAGE` and `_UNKNOWN_FAILURE` maps from the files router. A style point, not a defect: the messages match GET /files/{file_id} as intended.
Newest first with `file_id` as the tie-breaker is the intended order, not a mistake.
Another owner's class answers 404 class_not_found, the same as a missing class. Intended (owners must not learn of each other's classes).
`per_page` is capped at 100 and `page` must be at least 1; FastAPI answers 422 outside those bounds. Intended.
No migration or index is added; `files_class_idx` on files(class_id) already exists.
`list_class_files` calls `class_exists` and then a second query, so a class deleted in between could give an empty list. There is no class deletion in the app, so this cannot happen.
`status` is limited by a Literal in the route, so an unknown status answers 422 before reaching the library.
`created_at.isoformat()` includes the timezone offset; that is valid ISO 8601.
